headline: 22 days of total leave: Cabinet approves next year's holiday list
summary: The list includes 15 days of general holidays and 14 days of executive order holidays, totaling 22 days when combined with weekly holidays.
details: The Cabinet has approved the holiday list for the upcoming year. The list consists of 15 days of general holidays and 14 days of executive order holidays.
When combined with weekly holidays, the total number of effective holidays will be 22 days.
The decision was made during a Cabinet meeting held on Monday at the Secretariat, presided over by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani announced the details of the holiday list during a press conference following the meeting.
caption:
Planning your next year? The Cabinet has officially approved the holiday list, totaling 22 effective days off!

The Cabinet has approved the holiday list for the upcoming year. The list consists of 15 days of general holidays and 14 days of executive order holidays.

The decision was made during a Cabinet meeting held on Monday at the Secretariat, presided over by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

headline_marked: 10 Barishal routes hit as [[bus services suspended over three-wheeler dispute]]
headline: 10 Barishal routes hit as bus services suspended over three-wheeler dispute
summary: Thousands of passengers, including students, are stranded as the Barishal Bus Owners Association demands a ban on yellow three-wheelers.
details: Bus services on 10 routes connecting Barishal Sadar with various upazilas have been suspended, leaving thousands of commuters stranded.
The Barishal Bus Owners Association called for the suspension, demanding a total ban on yellow three-wheelers operating on the roads.
Around 60 buses on routes including Bakerganj, Bauphal, Charamaddi, Nehalganj, and Saheberhat have stopped operating.
Bus owners allege that three-wheeler operators felled trees on the roads to block buses, though three-wheeler drivers deny this, claiming it is a tactic to pressure for the ban.
The disruption began with several hours of service interruption yesterday before the full suspension took effect this morning.
Students from Barishal Government Women's College and BM College reported being unable to attend classes or get home due to the lack of transport.
Mohammad Shahidul Alam, officer-in-charge of Bandar Police Station, has called representatives from both sides to a meeting to resolve the dispute and restore services.
caption:
Thousands of passengers stranded in Barishal as 60 buses stop running over a dispute with three-wheelers.

Bus services on 10 routes connecting Barishal Sadar with various upazilas have been suspended, leaving thousands of commuters stranded.

The Barishal Bus Owners Association called for the suspension, demanding a total ban on yellow three-wheelers operating on the roads.

Around 60 buses on routes including Bakerganj, Bauphal, Charamaddi, Nehalganj, and Saheberhat have stopped operating.

Bus owners allege that three-wheeler operators felled trees on the roads to block buses, though three-wheeler drivers deny this, claiming it is a tactic to pressure for the ban.

The disruption began with several hours of service interruption yesterday before the full suspension took effect this morning.

Students from Barishal Government Women's College and BM College reported being unable to attend classes or get home due to the lack of transport.

Mohammad Shahidul Alam, officer-in-charge of Bandar Police Station, has called representatives from both sides to a meeting to resolve the dispute and restore services.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune
